prompt_text: What are the best online courses for learning shadow work and spiritual practice?
answer_verbatim:
Great question — “shadow work” and “spiritual practice” overlap a lot but come from different traditions (Jungian/psychological, somatic/trauma-informed, mindfulness/nondual, energy/yoga). Below I’ve grouped reputable, practical online options by approach so you can pick what fits your goals and safety needs.

Important safety note first
- Shadow work can bring up intense emotions and old trauma. If you have a history of complex trauma, severe depression, self-harm, or active psychiatric symptoms, do this work with a licensed therapist or trauma‑informed clinician present. Many programs recommend or require professional support for deeper levels of work.

Jungian / depth-psychology (shadow-focused)
- Jung Platform — A reliable hub for Jungian courses (shadow, dreamwork, archetypes) taught by certified analysts and scholars. Good if you want classic Jungian theory + practical exercises.
- Sounds True (Jungian teachers) — hosts courses and audio programs by Jungian-inspired teachers (e.g., James Hollis, David Richo). Good for reflective, meaning‑making shadow work.

Parts/“inner parts” (practical for shadow integration)
- IFS Institute (Internal Family Systems) — the originator of IFS offers online workshops and trainings. IFS is highly usable for working with “parts” that often live in the shadow. If you want a therapeutic, evidence‑based model for integration, start here.
- Online IFS intro workshops & certified IFS therapists — look for introductory courses before committing to professional training.

Trauma‑informed somatic and body‑based work
- Somatic Experiencing (SE) — SE trainings (intro workshops and longer programs) teach body-based regulation for trauma that often underlies shadow material. Good if your shadow work brings strong physical activation.
- Wim Hof Method (online) — breath and cold-exposure practices for embodied regulation; useful alongside shadow work for building resilience (not a trauma therapy).

Mindfulness, meditation, and evidence-based foundations
- Palouse Mindfulness (free MBSR) — a well-regarded online MBSR course (free, self-paced). Great foundation for emotional regulation and presence before deeper shadow exploration.
- Coursera (e.g., The Science of Well-Being by Yale / various mindfulness courses) — accessible, evidence-based introductions to habit change, wellbeing, and basic contemplative practice.
- Tara Brach & Jack Kornfield courses (their sites / Sounds True / Insight Timer) — RAIN technique and compassion practices that are very helpful when painful shadow material surfaces.

Spiritual / nondual / contemplative traditions
- Teachers like Adyashanti, Rupert Spira, Eckhart Tolle — they offer online satsangs, programs, and retreats that shift identification and cultivate presence. Useful when your intention is spiritual awakening alongside psychological integration.
- Insight Timer, Waking Up (Sam Harris) — apps with guided meditations and short courses to develop daily presence.

Marketplaces & multi‑teacher platforms (wide variety, vary in quality)
- The Shift Network — lots of spiritual & shadow integration programs with experienced contemporary teachers; some are multi-module, some are short.
- Udemy — many practical shadow-work courses; quality varies—read reviews and instructor background carefully.

Free or low-cost starting points
- Intro articles + journaling prompts on Jung Platform, Tara Brach’s free guided meditations, and Palouse Mindfulness MBSR.
- Insight Timer — many free guided practices for grounding, RAIN, and shadow-oriented meditations.

How to choose the right course
- Clarify your goal: self-inquiry/insight, emotional healing, trauma integration, spiritual awakening, or a mix.
- Prioritize trauma‑informed teachers if you expect strong emotions.
- Look for credentials/experience, clear syllabus, student reviews, and somatic/grounding practices included.
- Start with a short intro course or free materials, then deepen to longer training if it resonates.
- Consider community / group integration sessions and 1:1 therapy/coaching for support.

Sample pathways
- For psychological, structured integration: start with an IFS intro + Jung Platform shadow course + daily mindfulness (Palouse MBSR).
- For somatic trauma resolution: do a somatic regulation course (SE intro or breathwork) + trauma-informed IFS or therapy.
- For spiritual/awakening emphasis: foundational meditation (Insight Timer / Waking Up) + a nondual teacher’s online program, paired with reflective shadow practices to prevent bypassing.

If you want, tell me:
- whether you’re mainly after psychological healing or spiritual awakening,
- any trauma history or current mental‑health concerns,
- and your budget/time availability.

I can then recommend 2–4 specific courses and a suggested 8–12 week learning plan tailored to you.
